title: 3.8 A Canadian nurse
unit_title: Meeting people and talking about them
unit_outcome: Introduce people and answer introductions, use the short forms of be, answer yes/no questions in short, compare ages, talk about languages, nationalities and jobs, describe people, say whose things are, give an address and say what you want to be.
goal: Put a nationality before a noun, with a or an and never with -s (Sofia is a Canadian nurse. / Luis is an American driver. / They're two Spanish men.).
grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 3.8 Canada and Spain: A1 says a nationality after be (I am Canadian.); A1+ 3.8 puts the nationality before a noun (a Canadian nurse). The one new grammar relationship is that word order, with an before American, and an adjective that never takes -s when its noun does (two Spanish men, never Spanishes). The cast's nationalities are A1's (Ana Mexican, Sofia Canadian, Luis American, Diego Spanish); the new work photos show Ana teaching, Sofia nursing and Luis driving a bus, and 1.5's photo of Diego and his brother in Spain. Picture banks change the job or the people; nationality is told apart in Listen.
prerequisite: A1 3.7-3.8 nationalities; A1 3.9 teacher, nurse, driver; A1 2.6 two; A1+ 1.5 brothers; A1+ 2.9 men and women; A1+ 3.2 I'm, we're; A1+ 3.3 they're.
speaking_outcome: Say an American as one group (a-nAmerican); stress the noun after the nationality. Do not require native-like speed.
